en.title: Romanian Quotation Marks
en.summary: Learn how Romanian quotation marks sit on the line and how to change your voice when reading them.

sections.title: The sound
paragraphs: Quotation marks show someone is speaking. They do not make a sound by themselves. Instead, they guide your tone. Your voice pauses slightly before quoted speech. Then your pitch changes to show spoken words. Listen to the greeting „(bună) /bu.ˈnə/!”. Your voice sounds bright and friendly here.

sections.title: How to say it
paragraphs: Pause briefly when you see the opening quote. Drop your voice slightly before the quote starts. Raise your pitch inside the quote to sound lively. For „(da) /da/”, push clear air through your open mouth. Stress the quoted word clearly. Lower your pitch again after the closing quote.

sections.title: Reading rules
paragraphs: Look closely at the marks on the page. The opening quote sits low on the baseline. It looks like two tiny commas. The closing quote sits high at the top. It looks like two raised apostrophes. Read „(pa) /pa/” with quotes around it to show a clear goodbye.

sections.title: Common mistakes
paragraphs: Do not place the opening quote up high. It always sits down at the bottom line. Do not read quoted words in a flat voice. A flat tone sounds like a robotic list. Give the quoted word real life with your pitch. Pause at the marks to let the listener breathe.
